scope: Independent adversarial static review of frozen M5 file CRUD; no runtime/Cargo or payload edits

findings.trigger: Multipart PATCH/PUT missing/filtered object or invalid lookup filter after successful lookup.begin
findings.evidence: raw(...).await? propagates before lookup.rollback().await. sqlx-core Transaction::drop260–273 only queues start_rollback; PgTransactionManager::start_rollback73–80 queues SimpleQuery, not awaited Ready. owned() returns known error and may release last Work/admission before queued rollback settles.
findings.effect: Runtime active may reach0 and shutdown returntrue while actual lookup rollback is outstanding. Existing callback missing-object ordering does not test physical rollback settlement.
findings.minimal_fix: Capture raw lookup result without ?, await lookup.rollback() on both success/error, THEN propagate original result. Keep rollback failure as StoreError::Database so owned marks readiness fault and retains guard on unknown transport.
findings.source_behavior_unchanged: Lookup still precedes multipart parsing; no extra SQL/pool or API behavior required.

bounded_clear_review: Auth4 task_sql_writer reuses original existing request grant; clones retain same permit through spawned request work/body/file/SQL. No new client/pool.
Caller cancellation detaches outer tokio task; Work is retained inside actual blocking save. No caller-owned JoinHandle abort in current paths.

Blocking file descriptors created with from_raw_fd immediately after openat; file and directory are lexical RAII owners. Awaited JoinError observes blocking closure completion; std-owned descriptors unwind before result. Subsequent create/update SQL errors explicitly await rollback except the prelookup finding. No unsupported claim that panic itself leaves a live file task was established.
Unknown non-database-server SQL failures and outer future panics fault/close runtime and deliberately retain Work; bounded shutdown returnsfalse, not synthetic retirement.
Runtime holds State/Notify/root only; Work holds Runtime and existingpermit. Auth retains Runtime but Runtime does not retain Auth/Bridge, so no new singleton reference cycle found.

Storage preserves orphan files on later DB failure/replacement/clear/delete and uses exclusive create/no-overwrite, default644, documented collision/all-suffix length semantics. Known unsupported file grammar/storage error domains remain scoped; no new requirements added.
